CVX.rationale: Chevron's fundamental trajectory has deteriorated sharply. Q1 2026 EPS of $1.11 represents a -44.5% YoY decline and -39% QoQ decline, with operating cash flow collapsing -51.6% YoY to just $2.51B (vs $9.38B in Q3 2025). Net margin has compressed from 7.8% a year ago to 5.9%, and ROE has fallen from 10.5% to 5.9%. The balance sheet has expanded significantly (total assets up to $329.5B from $256.4B a year ago, likely due to the Hess acquisition), but this has not translated into improved earnings power. Meanwhile, the stock is trading at a P/E of 34.3x — nearly double the 17.4x level from July 2025 and at the top of its 365-day range (16.8-34.8). This is an extreme valuation for a cyclical energy company experiencing earnings contraction. The P/B of 2.04 is also near the top of its range (1.5-2.1). Oil prices have been volatile and recently surged on geopolitical tensions (Houthi attacks, Iran blockade), but WTI at $93/bbl on July 23 is still below the $110+ levels seen in late April/early May, and the recent rally appears driven by supply disruption fears rather than sustainable demand growth. Analysts expect a strong Q2 2026 (EPS ~$5.79), but this is largely a function of easier YoY comps and timing items reversing — the underlying trajectory of the business is concerning. The combination of sharply deteriorating fundamentals, extreme valuation relative to history, and commodity price uncertainty creates a highly unfavorable risk/reward. Near-term catalysts (Q2 earnings on July 31) could actually disappoint given the Q1 weakness and the gap between analyst expectations and recent operational performance.
